patient_history: Patient is a 19-year-old female with a known history of asthma presenting with acute shortness of breath and wheezing after exposure to a cat, her known allergen trigger. She used her albuterol inhaler with minimal relief prior to arrival. On exam, bilateral expiratory wheezes were noted with mild use of accessory muscles. She was treated with nebulized albuterol and ipratropium, oral corticosteroids, and observed for two hours with significant improvement before discharge.
reference_summary: 19-year-old female with asthma developed an acute exacerbation after allergen exposure; treated with nebulized bronchodilators and oral corticosteroids with good response before discharge.

patient_history: A 29-year-old female presented to the emergency department with sudden onset of severe abdominal pain localized to the right lower quadrant, associated with nausea and low-grade fever. She denies any prior surgical history. On examination, there was rebound tenderness and guarding over McBurney's point. Ultrasound revealed a dilated, non-compressible appendix measuring 9mm. Patient was diagnosed with acute appendicitis and scheduled for laparoscopic appendectomy.
reference_summary: 29-year-old female with right lower quadrant pain, fever, and positive McBurney's point tenderness; ultrasound confirmed acute appendicitis, and she was scheduled for laparoscopic appendectomy.
